messages:
sana: FYI postdeploy quick-smoke for v0.24.0 canary (10%) — synthetic healthcheck is returning elevated 429s from the routing layer in us-west. attaching quick telemetry snapshot.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout started: v0.24.0 -> canary=10% (hosts: canary-usw2-07..12) :loudspeaker:
josh: spike observed at 09:46PT. 429s moved from ~0.1% -> 3.8% on healthcheck route /_health/synth. latency stays normal.
eva: log excerpt from envoy-proxy on canary-usw2-09:
```
[2026-03-21T09:46:12.123Z] "GET /_health/synth" 429 - upstream_cluster="route-kv" retry_count=2
[2026-03-21T09:46:15.456Z] "GET /_health/synth" 429 - upstream_cluster="route-kv" retry_count=0
```
eva: retries are configured tighter in v0.24.0 (retry backoff shortened). could be interacting poorly with rate-limiter token bucket.
ops-oncall: checking quota/rate metrics. Token bucket refill rate unchanged; I see a surge of healthcheck QPS from synthetic agent after the deploy (we started extra sampling). spike ~15 QPS per host.
qa-bot: synthetic-run summary: pre-deploy p99 success=99.98%, post-deploy p99 success=96.2%, error breakdown: 429=3.3%, 5xx=0.5%, other=0.0%.
sana: proposal: pause ramp and reduce canary to 2% (keep a small set for tracing) OR pin traffic to v0.23.x. Also we can temporarily adjust synth sampling to reduce probe QPS while we triage.
release-manager: prefer to avoid full rollback if it's a probes/telemetry amplification issue. can we throttle synth agents first and observe? that would reduce noise and help validate.
josh: agree with throttling probes first. I'll flip synth sampling to 0.2x for canary ring now.
ops-oncall: throttled synth: runbook command executed:
```bash
kubectl patch configmap synth-config -n infra -p '{"data":{"sample_multiplier":"0.2"}}'
```

ops-oncall: applying now — expect QPS drop in ~30s.
qa-bot: post-throttle sample (canary-usw2-07..12): p99 success=99.9%, 429=0.2% (sample window 2m). looks much better on hosts that received throttle.
josh: can confirm canary-usw2-11 still showing small 429 blip (0.9%) — not all hosts evenly adjusted due to rollout lag in configmap.
sana: action plan consensus: (1) pause ramp (no further percentage increases), (2) keep canary at 2% for tracing, (3) throttle synth sampling globally for canary rings while triage proceeds, (4) create ticket REL-2048 to investigate retry/backoff + rate-limiter interaction and to add a defensive circuit for healthchecks.
release-manager: noted. I'll attach release notes warning and mark the change-window as "held" in the calendar.
deploy-bot: Canary ramp paused per request by sana. Current canary=2% (hosts: canary-usw2-07..08).
ops-oncall: configmap rollout completed to all canary hosts. re-checking metrics.
qa-bot: final quick sweep: canary p99 success=99.92%, 429=0.18%, 5xx=0.1%. error pattern localized to older proxy config (canary-usw2-11) which was on slow kube-propagation but now cleared.
sana: thanks team. keeping pin to v0.23.x for production traffic and holding the change window. when REL-2048 has initial triage (root cause hypothesis), we'll re-open this thread for a controlled reattempt with adjusted retry/backoff defaults and a lower synth multiplier.
release-manager: creating REL-2048 and adding initial notes + telemetry links.
josh: quick note for runbook: add step to throttle synth agents before pausing ramp in similar future cases — saved us a rollback.
sana: agreed — adding that to the release checklist. closing handoff: ops will monitor 1h and report back here if any regressions.
